summary.text: Claude is a language model that Anthropic introduced in March 2023 together with the lighter Claude Instant, after a closed alpha with partners including Notion, Quora and DuckDuckGo. Businesses could request access through a chat interface and the API in Anthropic's developer console; in May 2023 Anthropic raised its context window from 9K to 100K tokens.

summary.text: Claude Instant is a language model that Anthropic introduced in March 2023 together with Claude, presenting it as the faster, lighter and lower-cost of the two versions. It was offered through Anthropic's API; this record covers the API versions claude-instant-1.0 and claude-instant-1.1.

contextWindowTokens.note: 100K tokens per prompt at launch. The model card states the model was trained for 200K tokens; full 200K support came with Claude 2.1.

changes.text: Launched with claude.ai, a public beta chat site for users in the US and UK; Claude had been offered through a console chat interface, the API and partner products.
Anthropic reports better coding, maths and reasoning than its previous models, and longer responses of up to a few thousand tokens in one go.
Trained on more recent data, according to Anthropic; the model card puts the end of the training data in early 2023.
Gave harmless responses more often than Claude 1.3 in Anthropic's internal red-teaming evaluation.

summary.text: Claude 2 is the successor to Anthropic's Claude language model, released in July 2023 through the API and claude.ai, a new public beta chat site open to users in the US and UK. It accepted prompts of up to 100K tokens, and Anthropic's model card describes it as an evolution of its earlier Claude models rather than a major change. It was later also offered on Amazon Bedrock.

changes.text: Anthropic reports gains over Claude Instant 1.1 in maths, coding and reasoning.
Gives longer, more structured responses and follows formatting instructions more closely, according to Anthropic, with better quote extraction and question answering.
Anthropic reports improved multilingual capabilities, without naming languages or figures.
Hallucinates less and resists jailbreaks better, according to Anthropic's automated red-teaming evaluation.

summary.text: Claude Instant 1.2 is an updated version of Claude Instant, which Anthropic positions as its quicker, lower-cost language model for tasks such as dialogue, text analysis, summarisation and document comprehension; it was released through the API in August 2023. Anthropic says it draws on strengths of Claude 2 and improves on Claude Instant 1.1 in maths, coding, reasoning and safety.

contextWindowTokens.note: On claude.ai the full 200K window was reserved for Claude Pro users at launch.

features.note: Offered as a beta feature at launch.

changes.text: Context window doubled from 100K to 200K tokens; on claude.ai the full window was reserved for Claude Pro users.
Tool use added as a beta API feature, letting developers define functions or APIs for the model to call.
System prompts introduced, so users can give the model custom instructions and set context such as a role.
Anthropic reports fewer false statements than Claude 2.0 and fewer incorrect answers about long documents.

summary.text: Claude 2.1 is an update to Anthropic's Claude 2 language model, released in November 2023 through the API and as the model behind claude.ai. It raised the context window to 200K tokens and added system prompts and a beta tool-use feature; the model card appendix says it builds on Claude 2.0 rather than being a new base model.

sources.locator: Model details; Long context and near-perfect recall

changes.text: Accepts images such as tables, graphs and photos next to text; the Claude 3 model card names multimodal input as a key enhancement of the family.
Anthropic says the Claude 3 models refuse borderline but harmless prompts less often than earlier Claude models.
Anthropic says it answers difficult open-ended factual questions correctly more often than Claude 2.1, and gives fewer incorrect answers.
Knowledge cutoff of August 2023, according to the Claude 3 model card.

summary.text: Claude 3 Opus is a language model from Anthropic that accepts text and images and responds in text. It was introduced with Claude 3 Sonnet and Claude 3 Haiku as the Claude 3 family, which Anthropic ordered by capability with Opus above the other two, and was offered through the Claude API and on claude.ai for Claude Pro subscribers.

changes.text: Adds image input next to text, which the Claude 3 model card names as a key enhancement of the family; output remains text.
Anthropic says it is about twice as fast as Claude 2 and Claude 2.1 for most workloads.
Anthropic says the Claude 3 models refuse borderline but harmless prompts less often than earlier Claude models.
Knowledge cutoff of August 2023, according to the Claude 3 model card.

summary.text: Claude 3 Sonnet is the middle model of Anthropic's Claude 3 family: a language model that accepts text and images, responds in text and, according to Anthropic, balances intelligence and speed for enterprise workloads. At launch it powered the free tier of claude.ai and was offered through the Claude API and Amazon Bedrock, with a private preview on Google Cloud Vertex AI.

changes.text: Adds image input next to text, which the Claude 3 model card names as a key enhancement of the family; output remains text.
Anthropic says the Claude 3 models refuse borderline but harmless prompts less often than earlier Claude models.
Knowledge cutoff of August 2023, according to the Claude 3 model card.

relations.note: Editorial link: Claude 3 Haiku took the fast, low-cost place in the lineup that Claude Instant held. The launch posts do not name a predecessor.

summary.text: Claude 3 Haiku is a language model from Anthropic that accepts text and images, positioned by Anthropic as the fast, low-cost model of the Claude 3 family for uses such as live customer chats and data extraction. Named on 2024-03-04 and released on 2024-03-13, it was offered through the Claude API, on claude.ai for Claude Pro subscribers and on Amazon Bedrock.

changes.text: Anthropic reports improved vision, for example in reading charts and graphs and in transcribing text from imperfect images.
Knowledge cutoff moved to April 2024, from August 2023 for the Claude 3 models.
Same list price as Claude 3 Sonnet: 3 USD per million input tokens and 15 USD per million output tokens.
Output of up to 8,192 tokens per response became available in beta on 2024-07-15 and without a beta header from 2024-08-19.

relations.note: Editorial link: the announcement presents Claude 3.5 Sonnet at the speed and cost of Claude 3 Sonnet, Anthropic's mid-tier model, without naming a predecessor.

summary.text: Claude 3.5 Sonnet is a language model from Anthropic that accepts text and images, the first release of its Claude 3.5 family. It was free on claude.ai and the Claude iOS app and offered through the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI; Anthropic says it kept the speed and cost of Claude 3 Sonnet and ran at twice the speed of Claude 3 Opus.

changes.text: Adds computer use in public beta: the model works with a computer by looking at a screen, moving a cursor, clicking and typing. Anthropic called the feature experimental.
Anthropic reports improvements across the board, especially in agentic coding and tool use, at the same price and speed as the June 2024 model.

summary.text: The October 2024 revision of Claude 3.5 Sonnet is an upgraded version of that Anthropic language model for text and image input, released under the same name but with its own API id, claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022. It introduced computer use as a public beta on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Anthropic says it kept the price and speed of the June 2024 model.

inputModalities.note: Text-only at release; image input added on 2025-02-24.

changes.text: Released for text input only, unlike Claude 3 Haiku, which accepted images; image input was added on 2025-02-24.
Knowledge cutoff moved to July 2024, from August 2023 for Claude 3 Haiku.
Anthropic highlights coding, improved instruction following and more accurate tool use, at a speed similar to Claude 3 Haiku.
Revised list price (update of 2024-12-03) of 0.80 USD per million input tokens and 4 USD per million output tokens, against 0.25 USD and 1.25 USD for Claude 3 Haiku.

lifecycle.note: Retired on the Claude API. The release notes say it remained available on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud.

summary.text: Claude 3.5 Haiku is a language model from Anthropic, presented as the next generation of its Haiku model at a speed similar to Claude 3 Haiku. It became available on the Claude API on 2024-11-04 as a text-only model, with image input added on 2025-02-24, and Anthropic also announced it for Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI.

changes.text: Adds an optional extended thinking mode that shows step-by-step reasoning before the answer; the standard mode remains available.
API users can set a thinking budget in tokens, up to an output limit that the announcement gives as 128K tokens.
Trained on public web data through November 2024, with a knowledge cutoff at the end of October 2024.

relations.note: The announcement presents the standard mode as an upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet without naming a snapshot; the October 2024 upgrade was the current Claude 3.5 Sonnet at the time.

summary.text: Claude 3.7 Sonnet is a language model in Anthropic's Sonnet line that accepts text and images and was offered in the Claude apps, on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI. Anthropic calls it a hybrid reasoning model: it gives standard answers or, in an extended thinking mode, shows its reasoning step by step.

It was offered to free and paid Claude users, on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, with near-instant answers and an extended thinking mode, and Anthropic presents it as an upgrade to Claude 3.7 Sonnet.

changes.text: Anthropic describes it as an upgrade on agentic tasks, real-world coding and reasoning; the release notes call it an incremental update.
Does not accept the temperature and top_p parameters in the same request; only one of the two may be set.

Anthropic calls it an incremental update to Opus 4 and deployed it under the same ASL-3 Standard.

It is offered in the Claude apps, on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Anthropic presents it as a drop-in replacement for Claude Sonnet 4 at the same price.

changes.text: Adds an extended thinking mode, a first for the Haiku line; the system card notes that Claude 3.5 Haiku had none.
Trained to keep track of how much of its context window it has used; the window was 200K tokens at release.

summary.text: Claude Haiku 4.5 is a language model in Anthropic's Haiku line of small, fast models that accepts text and images, with a 200K-token context window and an extended thinking mode. It is offered in the Claude apps, Claude Code, on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Anthropic presents it as a drop-in replacement for Claude 3.5 Haiku and Claude Sonnet 4.

lifecycle.note: Listed by Anthropic as a legacy model that is still available; retirement not sooner than 2026-11-24.

summary.text: Claude Opus 4.5 is a language model in Anthropic's Opus line that accepts text and images, with a 200K-token context window, extended thinking and an effort parameter for trading thoroughness against token use. It is offered in the Claude apps, on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry, at a lower price than earlier Opus models.

contextWindowTokens.note: The launch announcement offered the 1M token context window in beta; the model page lists 1M tokens.

changes.text: Anthropic says it is the first Opus-class model with a 1M token context window, offered in beta at launch and out of beta from 13 March 2026.
Adds adaptive thinking, in which the model decides how much to think, steered by the effort setting; manual thinking budgets are deprecated.
Adds context compaction in beta on the API, which summarises older context during long-running tasks.
Prefilling the assistant message is no longer supported.

summary.text: Claude Opus 4.6 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Opus line, released on 5 February 2026 on claude.ai, the Claude API and major cloud platforms. It takes text and image input, launched with adaptive thinking and with context compaction in beta, and has a 1M token context window that was in beta at launch.

contextWindowTokens.note: The launch announcement offered the 1M token context window in beta; the model page lists 1M tokens.

changes.text: Adds support for adaptive thinking alongside extended thinking.
Became the default model for Free and Pro plans on claude.ai and in Claude Cowork.
Anthropic reports improved resistance to prompt injection compared with Sonnet 4.5.

summary.text: Claude Sonnet 4.6 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Sonnet line, released on 17 February 2026 on all Claude plans, Claude Code, the Claude API and major cloud platforms at the same price as Sonnet 4.5. It takes text and image input, supports adaptive and extended thinking, and became the default model for Free and Pro users on claude.ai.

access.note: Invitation only, for Project Glasswing participants.

released.note: Made available on this date as an invitation-only gated research preview for Project Glasswing participants, not as a general release.

summary.text: Claude Mythos Preview is a general-purpose model that Anthropic announced on 7 April 2026 with Project Glasswing, a defensive cybersecurity initiative. It was offered as an invitation-only research preview for Glasswing participants through the Claude API and major cloud platforms; Anthropic said it did not plan general availability and later called it the first Mythos-class model.

changes.text: Accepts higher-resolution images, up to 2,576 pixels on the long edge instead of 1,568.
Uses an updated tokenizer; Anthropic says the same input can map to roughly 1.0 to 1.35 times as many tokens.
Ships with safeguards that automatically detect and block prohibited or high-risk cybersecurity requests.
Non-default values for temperature, top_p or top_k are no longer accepted and return an error.

summary.text: Claude Opus 4.7 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Opus line, released on 16 April 2026 across Claude products, the Claude API and major cloud platforms at the Opus 4.6 price. It accepts higher-resolution images and uses an updated tokenizer; Anthropic released it with safeguards that detect and block prohibited or high-risk cybersecurity requests.

changes.text: Accepts system messages sent mid-conversation, after a user turn, while keeping prompt cache hits.
Anthropic reports lower rates of misaligned behaviour than Opus 4.7 in its alignment assessment.
Anthropic says early testers found it more likely to flag uncertainty about its own work and less likely to make unsupported claims.

summary.text: Claude Opus 4.8 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Opus line, released on 28 May 2026 at the Opus 4.7 price and available on the Claude API and major cloud platforms. It takes text and image input with a 1M token context window, added mid-conversation system messages, and later served as the fallback for requests that Claude Fable 5's safeguards blocked.

changes.text: Open to all customers, whereas Claude Mythos Preview was an invitation-only research preview for Project Glasswing participants.
Priced at 10 USD input and 50 USD output per million tokens, which Anthropic says is less than half the Mythos Preview price.
Adaptive thinking is the only thinking mode; disabling thinking or setting a manual thinking budget returns an error.

summary.text: Claude Fable 5 is a language model in Anthropic's Fable line, launched on 9 June 2026 on the Claude apps, the API and major cloud platforms. Anthropic describes it as a Mythos-class model whose classifiers route some cybersecurity, biology and chemistry requests to Claude Opus 4.8. Access was suspended on 12 June 2026 under US export controls and restored on Anthropic's own platforms from 1 July.

changes.text: Priced at 10 USD input and 50 USD output per million tokens, against 25 and 125 USD for Mythos Preview.
Adaptive thinking is the only thinking mode; disabling thinking or setting a manual thinking budget returns an error.

news.title: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5

summary.text: Claude Mythos 5 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Mythos line, launched on 9 June 2026 alongside Claude Fable 5 and offered by invitation only through Project Glasswing to a small group of cyber defenders and infrastructure providers. Anthropic says it is the same underlying model as Fable 5 with safeguards lifted in some areas, deployed as an upgrade to Claude Mythos Preview.

changes.text: Adaptive thinking is on by default; manual extended thinking budgets, deprecated on Sonnet 4.6, now return an error.
Uses a new tokenizer; the release notes estimate about 30% more tokens for the same text, depending on the content.
Priced at 2 USD input and 10 USD output per million tokens, against 3 and 15 USD for Sonnet 4.6; the introductory price became standard on 10 August 2026.
Launched with cyber safeguards on by default, the same as on Claude Opus 4.7 and Opus 4.8.

summary.text: Claude Sonnet 5 is a language model that Anthropic calls the next generation of its Sonnet family, released on 30 June 2026 on all Claude plans, the Claude API and major cloud platforms, and made the default for Free and Pro users. It takes text and image input with a 1M token context window, has adaptive thinking on by default and launched with cyber safeguards enabled.

changes.text: Thinking is on by default, and it can be disabled only at effort high or below.
Cyber safeguards similar to Opus 4.8's, with stronger guardrails on binary vulnerability scanning, penetration testing and exploit generation; flagged requests fall back to Opus 4.8.
Became the default model on the Claude Max plan.

summary.text: Claude Opus 5 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Opus line, released on 24 July 2026 on all platforms at the same price as Claude Opus 4.8 and made the default model on Claude Max. It takes text and image input with a 1M token context window, has thinking on by default, and uses cyber classifiers that allow finding vulnerabilities in source code but block exploit generation.

changes.text: Cache reads cost 0.25 USD per million tokens, 0.025 times the input price instead of 0.1 times; input and output prices are unchanged.
Revised cyber safeguards allow vulnerability discovery; penetration testing, exploit generation and binary-based vulnerability scanning are still redirected to Anthropic's Opus models.
Forced tool choice (tool_choice types any and tool) returns an error; auto and none still work.
Generated text carries Anthropic's text watermark.

summary.text: Claude Fable 5.1 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Fable line and the successor to Claude Fable 5, released on 1 September 2026 on the Claude apps, the Claude API and major cloud platforms. Anthropic says it is the same model as Claude Mythos 5.1 with different safeguards; token prices match Fable 5, cache reads cost less, and its text carries Anthropic's watermark.

access.note: Invitation only, through Project Glasswing and Anthropic's trusted access programs.

changes.text: Offered through Project Glasswing and the Life Sciences Verification Program, at launch only to a set of US organizations; Anthropic plans to add it to its Cyber Verification Program.
Cache reads cost 0.25 USD per million tokens, and generated text carries Anthropic's text watermark.
Anthropic reports lower rates of reward hacking and of reaching for resources outside its test environment than Mythos 5.

lifecycle.note: Invitation only, through Project Glasswing and Anthropic's trusted access programs.

summary.text: Claude Mythos 5.1 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Mythos line and the successor to Claude Mythos 5, released on 1 September 2026 for Project Glasswing participants alongside Claude Fable 5.1. Anthropic says it is identical to Fable 5.1 but has more permissive safeguards for vetted organisations and individuals in cybersecurity and the life sciences. Access is by invitation only.

announced.note: First named in the Claude Opus 5.5 announcement as following within weeks; no release date was given.

lifecycle.note: Named by Anthropic as a forthcoming model; not released as of 2026-10-01.

summary.text: Claude Haiku 5.5 is a forthcoming model in Anthropic's Claude Haiku line, first named in the Claude Opus 5.5 announcement of 22 September 2026 as following within weeks. Anthropic says it is aimed at high-volume, cost-sensitive applications; on 1 October 2026 the models overview still listed Claude Haiku 4.5 as the current Haiku model.

changes.text: Priced at 4 USD input and 20 USD output per million tokens, down from 5 and 25 USD for Opus 5; cache reads cost 0.20 USD.
Thinking can no longer be switched off; its depth is set with the effort parameter.
Forced tool choice (tool_choice types any and tool) returns an error.
Deployed with safeguards similar to those on Claude Fable 5.1 and with Anthropic's output watermarking.

summary.text: Claude Opus 5.5 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Opus line and, according to Anthropic, the first model of its Claude 5.5 family, released on 22 September 2026 on all platforms. It costs less per token than Claude Opus 5, has adaptive thinking that cannot be switched off, is available with zero data retention and carries Anthropic's output watermarking.

changes.text: Adds safety classifiers that block reasoning extraction, which Anthropic says is a first for a Sonnet model.
Up-front thinking is turned off with the new between_tools setting instead of the disabled value, at high effort or below.
Forced tool use (tool_choice types any and tool) returns an error.
The older computer_20251124 computer use tool is not accepted on the Claude API and Google Cloud.

summary.text: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Sonnet line, released on 28 September 2026 on all platforms at the same price as Claude Sonnet 5; Anthropic calls it the second model of its Claude 5.5 family. Anthropic says it is the first Sonnet model with classifiers that block reasoning extraction, and its thinking blocks are tied to the account that produced them.
